tags.description: The National Motor Lifeboat School at the mouth of the Columbia River, in the area known as the "Graveyard of the Pacific," is the ideal training ground for Coast Guard coxswains to learn how to safely conduct rescues in the surf.
tags.name: NMLBS

tags.image: The Coast Guard 29-foot Response Boat Small is designed year-round operation in waters along coastal borders for port and waterway security, search and rescue, drug and migrant interdiction, National Defense missions, and environmental protection.
tags.name: 29 RBS

tags.description: The workhorse of the Heavy Weather Fleet, the Coast Guard 47-foot Motor Lifeboat is self-righting and self-bailing. A fast response boat for rescue operations in the most extreme weather conditions like breaking surf and high seas.
tags.name: 47 MLB

tags.description: The 52 foot Motor Lifeboats serve only in the Pacific Northwest, despite being sixty years old, Coast Guard Surfmen value their ruggedness, long endurance, and ability to tow vessels over the typically hazardous inlet bars.
tags.name: Triumph
